short: The final land battle of the second Persian invasion, where a united Greek army decisively defeated Persian forces.
full:
In August 479 BCE, a large alliance of Greek city-states, including Sparta, Athens, Corinth, and Megara, faced the remnants of Xerxes' invasion force under the command of General Mardonius near the Boeotian city of Plataea. After a protracted stalemate and complex manoeuvres that briefly fractured the Greek lines, the Spartan hoplites shattered the elite Persian infantry and killed Mardonius.

The victory effectively ended the Persian threat to mainland Greece. On the same day, according to tradition, the Greek fleet defeated the remnants of the Persian navy at Mycale in Ionia. The twin victories marked the beginning of the Greek counter-offensive, leading to the formation of the Delian League and the eventual liberation of Greek cities in Asia Minor from Persian control.
